slice: Kawasaki KX250 / KX450 / KX250X / KX450X 2020-2027: maker-confirmed aftermarket parts (Pro Circuit, Yoshimura, Akrapovic, Rekluse, Wiseco, TM Designworks, Kawasaki genuine), magazine/tester/forum setup feedback, and project builds. Platform boundaries: KX450 new gen 2024 (center exhaust, Rideology app, no couplers); KX250 updated 2021 and new gen 2025 (app, maps, KTRC); 2026 graphics-only; 2027 KX450F/KX250F revised.

products.product: KX FI Calibration Kit (Handheld)

fits.notes: Compatible-models list on Kawasaki Australia page
Compatible-models list (also KX450 50th Anniversary 2024). Page text: KX450 (19-25) requires Sub Harness 26011-0933 and Tube Clamp 92037-1794

products.what_it_changes: Kawasaki Australia: handheld controller that lets riders 'adjust engine characteristics, by rewriting actual data maps'; adjusts fuel injection and ignition timing by throttle position and rpm; seven preset settings; SD card map transfer; live engine status.
products.caveats: Page is internally inconsistent: description says fits KX250F 13-25 and KX450F 09-10/12-25, compatible-models list omits some years (e.g. KX250 2021, KX450 2021-2022). US kawasaki.com listing (item 999990615) exists in search but fetch failed. MXA says 2024+ KX450 Rideology app replaces the old $700 FI calibration kit, so the handheld kit is mainly relevant to 2019-2023 bikes and the 2021-2024 KX250 era; Kawasaki AU still lists 2024-2026 compatibility.

products.product: KX FI Calibration Kit (PC version)
products.what_it_changes: Kawasaki Australia: handheld controller plugs into ECU, 'rewriting actual data maps'; seven preset settings incl. richer/leaner fuelling, advanced/retarded ignition, hard/soft surfaces, beginners.
supporting_parts: Sub Harness and Bracket required on older KX250F/KX450F per page
products.caveats: US price cited by testers: $699.95 (Keefer 2022 KX250, MXA 2021 KX250); Ultimate Motorcycling 2023 KX250X cites $775. Not confirmed which kit version those prices refer to.

products.product: Vortex X10 ECU with Twisted Development custom mapping (KX450)
products.what_it_changes: MXA (Oct 31 2024): with Map 6 'third gear is back in the party'; claimed '20-percent more power' feel, biggest gains off throttle/bottom; cleaner, less vibration. Keefer (Feb 2024): 'almost 4 more horsepower' than stock ECU on dyno with PC muffler, airbox mods, ETS MX18 fuel.
supporting_parts: Fuel trim 2 across with stock pipe, 4 across with PC Ti-6 (MXA)
products.caveats: No part number seen. Maps cannot be changed while riding (MXA). Prices from magazine, not maker page.

products.product: Ti-6 Titanium System w/ carbon end cap (KX450F/X '24-26)
products.what_it_changes: Maker page makes no claims. MXA dyno: 58.6 hp vs 57.4 stock (rubber airbox plug removed both), +2-4 hp 5,500-9,700 rpm, no change off idle-5,500; 2 lb lighter than stock.
supporting_parts: Twisted Development mapping (fuel trim 4 across per MXA)
products.caveats: MXA quoted $1,396.95 (Apr 2025); maker page now $1,536.95. Flange nuts hard to reach (12mm swivel socket). A Ti-6 Pro (AMA/FIM sound) variant exists; its 2024+ KX450 item number not seen. Keefer: Ti-6 Pro gives more linear low end but less low end than regular Ti-6 on stock ECU.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Baseline for ~160-200 lb riders; same as 2025 baseline
feedback.observed: Fork initial stroke too soft -> rides mid-stroke, harsh on deceleration. Fix: one 5.2 N/mm spring on one side (5.1 avg).
feedback.measured: Fork 5.1 N/mm (one 5.2 side), height 2-3 mm, comp 10 out, reb 9 out. Shock 54 N/mm (56 for 190+ lb), sag 105 mm, LSC 10 out, HSC 1.25 turns out, reb 12 out.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: 24/25 valving differs from 2023; still wants more hold-up
feedback.observed: Initial fork stroke too soft, harsh on decel; spring swap + clickers address it.
feedback.measured: Fork 5.1 N/mm (stock 5.0), 2-3 mm, comp 10, reb 9. Shock 54 N/mm (56 opt. 190+ lb), 105 mm sag, LSC 10, HSC 1.25 turns, reb 12.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Spring rates unchanged from 2023 'but the valving is quite a bit different'.
feedback.measured: Fork 5.0 N/mm, 3 mm, comp 10, reb 11. Shock 54 N/mm (56 opt. 190+), 105 mm sag, LSC 12, HSC 1.25 turns, reb 11.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Dyno with rubber airbox plug removed for both stock and Ti-6
feedback.observed: Better throttle response and midrange ~6,000 rpm to peak; stock felt choked, hard to pull 2nd->3rd.
feedback.measured: 58.6 hp vs 57.4 hp stock; +2-4 hp 5,500-9,700 rpm; ~+2 hp to 11,500; no change idle-5,500; 2 lb lighter.

feedback.product: 2024 KX450 mods that worked (Vortex ECU, PC Ti-6/Ti-6 Pro, intake, Hinson clutch, REP suspension)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: ~30 h on bike; ETS MX18 fuel
feedback.observed: Vortex ECU mapped by Twisted Development: linear usable power, prefers 2nd in corners. Ti-6 Pro: more linear low end but less low end than regular Ti-6 on stock ECU. PC slip-on better than stock, lacks full-system mid-top. Open 3D-printed filter cage: better response/low end. Hinson clutch: longer plate life, wider engagement. 13/51 tried and rejected (hurt cornering). REP valving: fork holds up better in braking bumps, shock better HSC hold-up. Fork raised 3 mm for stability.
feedback.measured: Vortex 'almost 4 more horsepower' than stock ECU on dyno. Stock chain lasted ~15 h.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: 2024-2025 KX450 with PC Ti-6; 51T rear sprocket
feedback.observed: 'Third gear is back in the party'; ~'20-percent more power' feel, mostly bottom/off-throttle; cleaner, less vibration; feels closer to stock KTM 450SXF.
feedback.measured: Fuel trim 2 across (stock pipe), 4 across (PC Ti-6). 58.01 hp dyno figure reported (unclear stock or modified).

feedback.author: Donn Maeda (bio; no explicit byline)
feedback.conditions: First motos with USFS spark arrestor, then removed
feedback.observed: With arrestor: better throttle response, mid-range, pulls taller gears. Without: harder hit and pull on top - 'one of the most drastic ... gains ... with a slip-on'; low-end roll-on gain smaller. Louder, deeper.

feedback.author: ML512
feedback.conditions: ~55 h bike, mounts ~30 h; fresh Dunlop MX34; chain +1 link; Factory Connection revalve; airbox/ECU/pipe/clutch mods
feedback.observed: More planted at lean, more comfortable on braking entry, more compliant exiting ruts under power; gains real but not dramatic.
feedback.measured: Went 1 click stiffer fork compression and 1 click faster rebound to hold ride height. Torque: Ti front 22 ft-lb (M8)/35 ft-lb (M10).

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Back-to-back at Glen Helen, sand track, Cal City; square edges and chatter; re-valved suspension
feedback.observed: More small-bump compliance, freer under load, better rear tracking, braking bumps less harsh; not wallowy; small loss of front traction at initial lean.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Stock bikes set for ~165 lb novice per MXA
feedback.observed: Stock Showa comfortable but too soft for heavier/faster riders. Fork: better ride height/balance without losing turning. Shock: more connected, smoother on chatter. Linkage: softer initial, quicker through stroke.
feedback.measured: Re-valve $900; linkage $465; +0.1 kg/mm shock spring recommended with linkage.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: FMF 4.1 vs PC Ti-6 full: PC more low end, FMF more mid. PC high-comp piston (needs VP T4+): more bottom torque, quicker low-end, stronger mid hit, better starts. Twin Air PowerFlow/airbox mods: quicker response, better top-end breathing, less heat. Twisted reflash or Vortex X10: more mid pull in 2nd/3rd, more over-rev. 51T for tight tracks. FCP Race Cups + engine mounts calm stiff chassis.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: California and Georgia tracks; unchanged bike for 2026
feedback.observed: Great front traction, chassis a bit stiff. Running fork flush and faster rebound vs 2025 baseline improved corner-entry stability and reduced oversteer.
feedback.measured: Fork 5.0 N/mm, flush, comp 8, reb 9. Shock 54 N/mm, 104 mm sag, HSC 2 turns, LSC 11, reb 10.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: Green coupler best all-round; black smooths and loses 1-2 hp 6,000-11,500; white same hp, crisper, slightly less over-rev. Forks too soft, bottom hard; adding compression only adds harshness. Rear brake grabby. Chain roller wears fast.
feedback.measured: 56.9 hp @ 9,500 rpm. Fork 5.1 N/mm, comp 12, reb 12, 2 mm up. Shock 54 N/mm, HSC 1.25 turns, LSC 18, reb 12, sag 105 mm. Launch control cuts up to 4 hp above 7,000 rpm.

feedback.product: 2022 KX250 couplers + 'Chavez map' via FI Calibration Kit
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: White and black couplers each help some areas with drawbacks; preferred custom 'Chavez map' (white ignition + black fuel) added midrange and extended top.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: Black coupler strongest low end but signs off early; white strongest mid-top but excessive engine braking (disagrees with Keefer 2020 description). Custom Chavez map: more low snap, no top loss. Fork harsh mid-stroke; front high, pushes. 51->52T kept out of 1st in corners. Two clicks more rebound fixed rear kick.
feedback.measured: Fork 4.9 N/mm, comp 8 out (stock 12), reb 12 (11), standard height, oil -5 to -10cc. Shock 54 N/mm, 103 mm sag, HSC 1.5 turns, LSC 10, reb 13 (15).

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Green coupler most usable; white better low-end recovery for slower corner entry but less top (conflicts with MXA 2021 KX250 description); black for extreme hard pack/loose, beginner friendly. Shock rode low under acceleration.
feedback.measured: Fork comp 12, reb 9, height 5 mm. Shock LSC 5, HSC 1.25 turns, reb 15, sag 103-104 mm. Gearing 13/50; 13/51 for heavier/slower riders.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: Wants more top end/torque; oversteer and head shake at speed; small airbox, flat filter flows too little. Sliding forks down (flush) fixes head shake and oversteer; +1 chain link and wheel back calms rough; full-coverage skid plate caused ignition cover damage/oil leaks.
feedback.measured: 58.27 hp (5th of 7). Weight 239 lb no fuel. MSRP $10,399. Launch control retards above 7,000 rpm to 3rd. App map in 'light on' slot detuned 15%.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: 6th of 7. 'Feels like a KX350'; closed airbox hurts response; second-gear bike in corners; Brembo front praised; app range slightly wider for 2025; new domed filter 'doesn't seal as well' as Twin Air; side-cover gasket leaks, water-pump seal failure, bolts strip.

feedback.author: Swapmoto staff
feedback.observed: 4th overall (scores 3-4-2-3-3). Handling best-in-class per several testers; aggressive app map gave noticeable gain - testers felt 2025 with that map stronger than a 2024 with airbox mod + aftermarket exhaust. Fork soft for some (Alex Ray).

feedback.author: Trevor Hunter
feedback.observed: DT-1 screenless cage + domed filter: more pull, better response. FMF 4.1 slip-on (quiet insert): power top to bottom, crisper. PC Ti-6: more aggressive delivery. Drilled airbox similar to DT-1 gain. Forks flush helped stability and braking. Chain +1 link improves stability/shock action.
feedback.measured: Gearing: stock 13/50; desert 13/47-48; trees 13/51-52. IMS 2.8 gal ~60 fast desert miles.

feedback.author: Ron Lawson
feedback.conditions: Off-road; softer X valving, AT81 tires, 18-in rear
feedback.observed: Softer off bottom, revs longer like a 250F; lacks stability at speed, twitchy under hard braking; runs hot in tight trails. Stiffened fork + couple clicks rebound to cut dive; Rideology map 'brings some bark back to the low end'.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Fork harsh on faster terrain; flush-3 mm helped twitchiness; shock bottoms in whoops -> add HSC 1/2-3/4 turn. Black coupler best throttle feel; green/white more low end but didn't fix jerky initial throttle. Used Kawasaki CHA map via FI Calibration Tool.
feedback.measured: Sag 104-106 mm, fork 3 mm. Stock 51T rear; 48-49T for fast GP.

feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Aggressive map; PC-modified bike also ridden
feedback.observed: Unchanged except graphics vs 2025. Forks harsh out of box, engine slightly 'choked' and less revvy than earlier KX250s; 240 lb wet. PC-modified bike: more snap, freer revving.
feedback.measured: Fork 2 clicks softer than stock; shock HSC in 1/4 turn.

feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Fox Raceway, standard map, 180 lb rider
feedback.observed: Fork too soft ('push, push, push, tuck'), harsh on landings; dropping fork flush improved front grip and high-speed stability; firmed all fork settings.

feedback.brand: multiple (Race Tech, Factory Connection, OEM springs)
feedback.author: quadzrulebro, crc245, Trailturd, MX529, Golfnut721, MXer391
feedback.observed: quadzrulebro (215 lb): OEM 5.2 fork springs + Race Tech Gold Valve, +25 ml oil, forks 3 mm up stopped bottoming but less plush. crc245 (180 lb): stock springs, +25cc fork oil + clickers made forks 'much happier'. Trailturd (190-195 lb, KX450X): swapped X springs 4.8/52 to KX450 5.0/54, 350cc oil, first clamp line, Precision Concepts revalve; Nissin brake swap best upgrade. MX529: FC 5.7 rear spring + revalve.
feedback.measured: gscx raised TPS 0.58 -> 0.6.

feedback.author: dancolvin633, shortty761
feedback.observed: PC full + Twin Air + Vortex (Pro6 map): 'decent' but less power than 2021-2024 KX250 with same mods; 51T improved handling. High-comp piston most-suggested next fix.

feedback.author: Don Williams
feedback.observed: Coupler swapping inconvenient; first gear too tall for technical terrain; suspension plush, some bottoming on downhills; Dunlop AT81 clog in mud. Suggests more compression for MX, steering damper for desert.
feedback.measured: FI Calibration Kit cited at $775.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Stock fork too soft on decel; settings add support while keeping comfort.
feedback.measured: Fork 5.1 N/mm (5.2 for 200+ lb B riders), comp 11-12 (13 with 5.2), reb 10-11, 3 mm. Shock 54 (56 for 190+), sag 105, LSC 15, HSC 1 1/8 turns, reb 11.

builds.title: 2024 KX450 Update And Mods That Have Worked

parts.product: Vortex ECU custom map (ETS MX18 fuel)

parts.observed: More linear low end; less low end than regular Ti-6 on stock ECU

parts.product: Filters + open 3D-printed cage, airbox grommet removed, side panel drilled
Clutch kit (basket, hub, pressure plate, plates)
parts.observed: Longer plate life, slightly wider engagement
Fork holds up better in braking bumps; shock better HSC/rear hold-up

common_first_mods: Remove the rubber airbox plug / open or drill the airbox cover on 2024+ KX450 (MXA 2024 race test; Keefer 2024; Dirt Bike Test 2026 KX450X). For 2025 Kawasaki removed the plug from production (MXA 2025 shootout).
Aftermarket exhaust - Pro Circuit Ti-6 or FMF 4.1 (MXA, Keefer, Dirt Bike Test, Swapmoto); on 2025 KX250 Keefer says PC = more low end, FMF = more mid.

ECU remap: Twisted Development reflash or Vortex X10 (MXA, Keefer); on 2024+ KX450/2025+ KX250 try the Rideology app aggressive map first - Swapmoto found a 2025 KX450 on the aggressive app map stronger than a modified 2024.

Fork spring/clicker changes on KX450: one 5.2 N/mm spring on one side (Keefer 2025/2026), or slide forks flush in clamps (MXA 2024, Cycle News 2025, Dirt Bike Test 2026 KX450X) - note Keefer runs 2-3 mm up; sources disagree on fork height.
Gearing: +1 tooth rear (51T) on KX450 (MXA 2024) and KX250 (Keefer 2025, MXA 2021 went 51->52); Keefer rejected 13/51 on 2024 KX450 because it hurt cornering.
Chain one link longer to move axle back for stability (MXA 2024, Dirt Bike Test KX450/KX450X builds).
Replace stock chain roller/guide with TM Designworks parts (MXA 2021 KX250, MXA 2022 KX450).
Engine mounts: Kawasaki optional softer uppers 32190-0917/-0918 or FCP mounts on 2024+ KX450 (Keefer, MXA, Vital MX).
Screenless/domed air filter cage (DT-1, Twin Air PowerFlow) (Dirt Bike Test, Keefer, MXA).

Hinson maker site gave no KX fitment/SKU; Works Connection Hinson page had SKUs but no year mapping.
No 2024+ KX450 piston from Wiseco, Vertex, JE or Pro-X confirmed; Wiseco RE822M09600 stops at 2023.
Pro Circuit Ti-6 Pro item numbers for 2024+ KX450 and 2025 KX250 not seen (page fetch errors).
